'''Sanagara''', is a [[Wikipedia:Unitary_parliamentary_republic|unitary semi-presidential republic]] located in western [[Massir]]. The country is composed of [[Eight federated state|eight federated states]] and [[three autonomous city territories]]. It occupies the majority of the [[Manu Peninsula]], as well as [[several smaller islands]] in the [[Ayre Archipelago]], and shares a land border with [[Dahe]] to the north and a maritime boundary with [[Oyreain]] to the southwest. The capital and largest city is [[Koyaya]], which also serves as the political, economic, and cultural center of the country. As of the most recent census, Sanagara has a population exceeding 38 million, making it the [[List of countries and dependencies by population|36th most populous country in the world]].

Sanagara traces its historical origins to the [[Shuese Empire]], which dominated the region during antiquity, and later to a kingdom established in the 10th century CE. By the 11th century, much of what is now Sanagara came under the influence of the [[Dahen dynasties]], lateron a colony of as the [[Siana|Sianan Empire]]. During The [[Red war]], the territory that now comprises Sanagara, then part of [[Siana|Sianan]] [[Samassa]], was occupied by the [[Dahe|Dahen Republic]] during the regional conflict known as the [[Red War]]. Following the end of the conflict and a brief period of reoccupation by [[Siana]], the country declared its independence in 1717. In the aftermath of the [[Sinian Revolution]], independent Sanagara unified with eight distinct colonial entities to form the present-day [[Wikipedia:Federal_republic|federal republic]]. In August 1719, the island territory of [[Kerash]] became the center of an international crisis when it was invaded by [[Oyreain]] amid a dispute over newly drawn [[Wikipedia:Maritime_boundary|maritime boundaries]]. A brief military engagement ensued before intervention by Dahe and other major powers led to a brokered ceasefire and the establishment of a demilitarised zone.

Sanagara combines elements of both [[Wikipedia:Parliament|parliamentary]] and [[Wikipedia:Presidential_system|presidential systems]]. Executive power is shared between the High Minister, who serves as head of state, and the Low Minister, who acts as head of government. Sanagara has a [[Wikipedia:World_Bank_high-income_economy|high-income economy]] and a robust [[Wikipedia:wiki/Industrial_technology|industrial]] base. In the 1730s, the country underwent a major transformation from a [[Wikipedia:Protectionism|protectionist]] regime to a [[Wikipedia:Liberalization|liberalised]], market-oriented economy. Today, the industrial sector remains the backbone of [[Sanagara's economic output]], followed closely by the [[Wikipedia:Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy |services sector]], agriculture, and a thriving [[World Tourism rankings|international tourism industry]]. Sanagara is notable for being the first country in [[Massir]] to introduce a [[Wikipedia:Minimum_wage|minimum wage]] and for enshrining [[Wikipedia:Women%27s_suffrage|women’s suffrage]] in its post-independence constitution. The country consistently ranks highly in international indices related to [[List of countries by Krali Total Development Index|quality of life]], human rights, and [[Wikipedia:Open_government|government transparency]], and is recognised for having one of the [[Corruption Perceptions Index|lowest levels of perceived corruption globally.]]

Sanagara maintains a [[Dahe-Sanagara relations|strong diplomatic and economic relationship]] with its eastern neighbor, [[Dahe]], who it shares deep historical and cultural ties stemming from centuries of [[Dahe|Dahen]] [[Wikipedia:Tributary_state|tributary statis]]. The two countries collaborate closely on trade, security, and regional development. Sanagara is an active member of [[various international organisations]], including regional trade blocs, intergovernmental councils, and global forums dedicated to peace, development, and [[Wikipedia:Climate_resilience|climate resilience]].
